messages.author: 0b86ca0cb4b615b0
messages.subject: Re: [camtrapR] Problem with the output of detectionHistory
parts:
Hi Maca,

this is expected behaviour. Please see Vignette 3, under "Handling of incomplete occasions".

https://cran.r-project.org/web/packages/camtrapR/vignettes/camtrapr3.html#Occupancy_analyses

One of the reasons for NA instead of 0 in detection histories is that 0 is considered a non-detection, which assumes there was a chance of detecting the species. With practical terms, with effort = 0, there is 0 chance of detecting a species. But, in terms of the model, even with effort = 0, the detection probabilities at those occasions are > 0, because the probabilities in the occupancy models can't be 0 or 1 due to the logit transformation.

So, the danger with 0 detection histories when there was 0 effort is that the model would assume that there was a small chance of detecting the species, when in reality it was 0. Therefore, using NA instead of 0 prevents the models from using cells with no effort, and thus ensures the probabilities are estimates correctly (using only cells for which there was at least some effort).

In mathematical terms, say you use effort as a covariate on detection probability, The logit of the detection probability is:

logit(p) = beta_0 + beta_1 * effort

beta_0 is the intercept, beta_1 is the effect of effort (in days). With effort = 0 (cameras not operating), we get:

logit(p) = beta_0

No matter how small we choose beta_0 (or rather, how small the model estimates it to be), the resulting detection probability at effort = 0 will not be 0 due to the logit transformation, thus allowing for detections when they were impossible.

I believe that was the main reasoning behind this admittedly confusing design choice. Does that answer your question?

Best regards,

Jürgen
